notes: DISCOVERED during the nahb-hmi-2026-10-19 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-06). The calendar tracks the November and December G.17 releases and stops there; the October one is missing, and it is the single release this corridor most needs, for two reasons. First, it is load-bearing evidence for the event that found it: the nahb-hmi-2026-11-17 lane measured that the entire pre-open lift on an HMI morning belongs to the 09:15 G.17 and not to the 10:00 HMI (34 stacked HMI days, SPY overnight gap 0.4828% vs a 0.3275% clean baseline, p=0.0385; the 44 unstacked days 0.3391%, p=0.85), and it could not verify whether October 2026 was stacked because the URL it tried 404s. It is not — G.17 lands 10-16, three days before the HMI — and that is what makes nahb-hmi-2026-10-19 the corridor's unstacked control. Second, it corrects the calendar's own count of 2026-10-16: that morning is already tracked as import/export prices, October opex and the Treasury primary-dealer agenda, and this session's reproduction says a G.17 morning is measurably wider than a clean one on its own (74 G.17 days, SPY gap p=0.0219 in the sibling's pass; this session reproduces the stacked cell at p=0.0365 on an independently parsed date set). An untracked 09:15 print sitting inside an opex Friday is the kind of stack this calendar exists to see. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry, and the proposing lane's own call is stand aside on every horizon.
